name: JnJ Patreon
description: Jimmy & Joe AI Podcast — Patreon Arcade, every cabinet unlocked
_why_a_second_manifest: Osimo 2026-08-24: installed from /patreon-arcade, the Chrome install prompt read name 'JnJ Arcade' (the shared manifest.json's name) and start_url '/' launched him into the free main arcade with Patreon games showing as locked teasers instead of back into the Patreon experience he installed from. manifest.json's start_url is hardcoded '/' — every page that links it always launches there regardless of which page triggered the install.
_why_scope_stays_broad: The prior /lock-in rule (feedback_ios_standalone_needs_meta_every_page addendum) says a per-page/second manifest can make iOS/Chrome treat that page as a DIFFERENT app than the one currently installed, ejecting the user to a browser view on navigation. That failure was traced to a NARROW/implicit scope on the second manifest (flap-fight.webmanifest, reverted). This manifest deliberately keeps scope:"/" identical to manifest.json's — same site-wide territory, only start_url and name differ — so navigating from an installed Patreon icon into any game (which lives outside both /patreon and /patreon-arcade, at /games/*) stays recognized as the same in-scope app rather than kicking out to a browser view. Verified live via serviceWorker registration + manifest fetch checks; genuine install-and-launch behavior on a real device could not be verified from here.
